items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: They wouldn't care if it was P.T. Barnum himself there.

ctx.x: It was a terrific drawing attraction. And that went on all across the country, from New York right into Los Angeles, San Francisco -- all the theatres was lined up around the block with people.

Only one theatre they didn't break the record in. That was Omaha, Nebraska. It was fifteen below zero there, and them people there didn't care who was in town. They wouldn't care if it was P.T. Barnum himself there. They wouldn't come out no fifteen below zero to see nothin'! You could throw a baseball in the theatre and wouldn't hit anybody, and nearly a whole week nobody showed up, except the shows. Heh-heh.
Now, tell me about what the Ink Spots were like.
